# Safe Isolated Agent Development with Orchestration

**What this answers:** How to safely run AI coding agents that perform risky work (destructive tests, experimental code, force-pushes) without endangering the host or production — with an orchestrator managing the fleet.

**Research date:** 2026-04-12 | **Sources:** [50 citations](citations.md)

---

## TL;DR

For a developer workstation running Claude Code agents on your own code: **Podman rootless containers with `--cap-drop ALL` + `--dangerously-skip-permissions` inside the container + a shell-loop orchestrator** is proportional to the risk. The container IS the security boundary — the agent can do anything inside its sandbox but cannot reach the host. Add `--network none`, `--read-only`, and `--pids-limit` to harden further.

For untrusted code or multi-tenant scenarios: upgrade to Firecracker microVMs or Kubernetes Agent Sandbox with gVisor/Kata.

## Key Comparison: Isolation Technologies

| Technology | Isolation | Boot | Overhead | Best For |
|-----------|-----------|------|----------|----------|
| Podman rootless | Process + user NS | <100ms | None | Dev workstation, own code |
| gVisor | User-space kernel | <100ms | 10-30% I/O | Multi-tenant, CI/CD |
| Firecracker | Hardware (own kernel) | 125ms | <5 MiB/VM | Untrusted code |
| Kata Containers | Hardware (via VMM) | ~200ms | Higher | Regulated industries |
| Managed Agents | Anthropic-managed | N/A | $0.08/hr | Zero infra teams |

## Key Comparison: Orchestrator Patterns

| Pattern | Complexity | Crash Recovery | Isolation |
|---------|-----------|----------------|-----------|
| Shell loop (Ralph Wiggum) | Low | Filesystem re-read | OS-level (containers) |
| Temporal | High | Automatic checkpoint | Activity-level |
| LangGraph | Medium | Optional checkpoint | None (shared process) |
| Agent SDK subagents | Low-Medium | --resume by session | Context-level or worktree |
| agtx / dmux | Medium / Low | Artifact polling / git | Worktree + tmux |

## Decision Framework

1. **Running your own agents on your own code?**
   → Podman rootless + shell loop. Container boundary is sufficient. [24][43]

2. **Running untrusted or third-party generated code?**
   → Firecracker microVMs or K8s Agent Sandbox with gVisor. [1][2][5]

3. **Need crash-safe orchestration across hours/days?**
   → Temporal workflows with durable human approval waits. [8][18]

4. **Solo dev, want simplicity?**
   → Shell loop (Ralph Wiggum pattern) with persona files + 3-attempt retry. [30][43]

5. **Want different agents per phase (Claude for code, Gemini for research)?**
   → agtx (phase-based) or dmux (task-based). [28][29]

6. **No infra team, need managed solution?**
   → Claude Managed Agents ($0.08/hr) or E2B (Firecracker-backed). [25][32]
